ruleName: Actions That Improve Conditions Affecting the Stroke
title: Is it Allowed to Remove Dew or Frost from Your Line of Play?
question: Early on a cold morning, your ball is on the fairway. There is a layer of frost and dew on the grass between your ball and the hole. Before playing, you wipe the frost away with your towel to make the shot easier. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: This is allowed because dew and frost are temporary water.
This is allowed because you are only cleaning the grass.
You receive the general penalty because you improved the conditions affecting your stroke.

explanation: Dew, frost and water are not loose impediments, so you cannot deliberately remove them to improve the conditions affecting your stroke. Brushing away dew or frost from your line of play or the area where your club will swing is a breach of Rule 8. However, there is no penalty if you accidentally remove dew or frost while taking a normal stance or making your stroke.

juniorVersion.title: Can You Wipe Away Dew or Frost Before You Hit?
juniorVersion.question: It’s a chilly morning and your ball is on the fairway. There is shiny dew and frost on the grass between your ball and the hole. You use your towel to wipe off the dew and frost before you hit. What should happen?

choices.text: This is fine because dew and frost are just water.
This is fine because you are only cleaning the grass.
You get a penalty because you made it easier for yourself by wiping away the dew or frost.
You get one extra shot added to your score.

juniorVersion.explanation: You must not try to make your shot easier by wiping away dew or frost from where you will hit the ball. The rules do not let you brush away dew or frost to help you play. It’s okay if you move it by accident when you walk or swing, but not on purpose.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Tiny drops of water you see on the grass in the morning.
Ice that covers the grass when it’s very cold.
The short grass between the tee and the green.
Extra shots you get for breaking a rule.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show children grass with dew or frost, and practice playing shots without touching or brushing it away.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think dew and frost are loose things you can move, like leaves.
They might believe cleaning the grass is always allowed before a shot.
